source: Yang et al. (2024) SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
finding: Same model (GPT-4 Turbo), same task, only the environment interface changed. A designed interface beat a raw shell by a wide margin.
numbers: SWE-bench Lite N=300. Shell-only 11.0% resolved; default ACI 18.0%. Full result 12.5% on SWE-bench, 87.7% on HumanEvalFix.
quote: Actions should be simple and easy to understand for agents.
limits: One model, single run per cell, no variance reported. SWE-bench measures single issues.
agent_relevance: Strongest direct LLM test of the claim that the environment carries cognitive load. Design the program around the model as an environment.

source: Yang et al. (2024) SWE-agent ablations (HTML v3)
finding: Each interface choice moved the score. Linting on edit, summarized search, a 100-line viewer and a short history all helped. More raw information hurt.
numbers: Edit: none 10.3, no lint 15.0, lint 18.0. Search: none 15.7, iterative 12.0, summarized 18.0. Viewer: 30 lines 14.3, 100 lines 18.0, full file 12.7. Context: full history 15.0, last 5 obs 18.0, no demo 16.3.
quote: Guardrails mitigate error propagation and hasten recovery.
limits: Only GPT-4 Turbo; N=300; one-factor-at-a-time ablation, interactions untested.
agent_relevance: Concise, filtered environment feedback beats complete feedback. Matches guardrail-style design and a bounded context window.

source: Cognitive Workspace: Active Memory Management for LLMs (2025)
finding: An agent-managed external workspace reused stored material far more than plain retrieval. Authors cite Clark and Chalmers and Hutchins only as motivation.
numbers: Memory reuse 54.5% to 59.8% vs 0% for standard RAG; net efficiency 17-18%; 3.3x operation overhead; 8 documents, GPT-3.5-turbo; no accuracy reported.
quote: cognition distributes across individuals, artifacts, and time
limits: N not stated, huge effect sizes (d up to 196) from very few runs. Task quality not measured. Claimed 70% completion is a projection.
agent_relevance: Weak evidence. Shows the idea is being built, not that answers improve. Active management costs about 3x operations.

source: United Minds or Isolated Agents? Coordination of LLMs under Cognitive Load Theory (CoThinker, 2025)
finding: Spreading load over specialised agents with a shared transactive memory helped on hard tasks but hurt on instruction following.
numbers: LiveBench normalised to Flash-8B IO=1.00: Pro IO 1.85, CoT 1.79, MAD 1.92, DMAD 2.05, CoThinker 2.09. Instruction following Pro 0.95 vs IO 1.03. GPT-5 math 88.57 vs 82.63 IO; reasoning 81.88 vs 68.38.
limits: No variance or significance tests visible. Communication overhead adds extraneous load on execution tasks. First 100k of 160k characters read.
agent_relevance: Social setting reduces load only when the task is complex; on simple execution the social overhead costs more than it saves. Gate any multi-voice step.

source: CoThinker transactive memory and style ablation (Table 4)
finding: Removing the shared memory helped some models and hurt others. Role styles helped all three.
numbers: Math subset. Qwen3-30B: both on 81.87, no styles 69.79, no TMS 76.41. GPT5-Nano: 55.97, 49.02, 62.36. GPT-OSS-20B: 57.15, 48.21, 58.37.
limits: Authors blame models refusing to give intermediate reasoning. Single table, no seeds shown.
agent_relevance: Shared external memory works only if the model writes useful intermediate results into it. Role framing gave a steadier gain (+7 to +12 points) than shared memory.

source: CoThinker constrained-budget results (Table 3)
finding: Under an 8192-token budget the multi-agent load split gave very large gains.
numbers: Gemini-2.5 math 76.3 vs 59.3 IO, reasoning 69.2 vs 31.0. GPT-4.1 reasoning 70.8 vs 40.8.
limits: Greedy decoding; token budget may favour setups that split work. Not compared with equal-compute baselines like self-consistency.
agent_relevance: When one context is tight, splitting work across contexts may beat one long chain. Needs an equal-compute control before we trust it.

source: Shojaee et al. (2025) The Illusion of Thinking
finding: Reasoning models collapsed on Tower of Hanoi as disk count grew, even when the solving algorithm was given in the prompt.
numbers: Collapse near N=7-8 disks (255 moves at N=8). Models: Claude 3.7 Sonnet (thinking and not), DeepSeek-R1/V3, o3-mini. 64k max output. Giving the algorithm did not move the collapse point.
limits: Contested by c08. Output-length limits confound the result.
agent_relevance: Models are poor at holding a long move sequence in their head. Externalising the sequence to a program or store should help.

source: Lawsen (2025) Comment on The Illusion of Thinking
finding: Collapse is mostly an output-limit and grading artifact. Asking for a generating function instead of a move list fixed Hanoi. Some River Crossing items were unsolvable.
numbers: No accuracy table in abstract. Unsolvable River Crossing instances for N>5 (boat capacity). Reports high accuracy with function output.
limits: Preliminary check, small test. Model-coauthor claim removed in v2.
agent_relevance: A tool or program as the external place for the long sequence beats having the model write all steps. Direct example of the program as environment.

source: Nye et al. (2021) Show Your Work: Scratchpads for Intermediate Computation
finding: Letting the model write intermediate steps enables multi-step computation like long addition and program execution, even few-shot.
numbers: Abstract only; no accuracy figures retrieved (PDF unreadable).
limits: Tables not extracted. Written steps are still inside the model's own output.
agent_relevance: The earliest paper-and-pencil result for LLMs. The scratchpad is the model's external memory.

source: Gao et al. (2022) PAL: Program-aided Language Models
finding: The model writes code, an interpreter does the arithmetic. This beat chain-of-thought from a much larger model.
numbers: 13 tasks. GSM8K with Codex beat PaLM-540B CoT by 15 points absolute top-1.
limits: Per-task numbers not read. Needs problems that can be written as code.
agent_relevance: Offloading calculation to the environment is a measured win. Use the interpreter for any exact step.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager: open-ended embodied agent with LLMs
finding: A persistent library of executable skills, built from the environment, lifted exploration in Minecraft.
numbers: 3.3x more unique items, 2.3x longer distances, tech-tree milestones up to 15.3x faster than prior best.
limits: Abstract-level numbers; Minecraft only; GPT-4 dependent.
agent_relevance: A skill library is memory held in the world, not in weights. Fits an agent that stores working methods outside the model.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager ablations (HTML v2)
finding: Removing the curriculum or self-verification cut discovery sharply. No skill library made progress plateau late.
numbers: Random curriculum: items -93%. No self-verification: -73%. GPT-3.5 for code: GPT-4 gets 5.7x more unique items. Skill library removal: plateau, no percentage in text.
limits: Numbers for some ablations only in a figure. First 100k of 148k characters read.
agent_relevance: Feedback from the environment (verification) matters as much as the stored skills.

source: Yao et al. (2022) ReAct
finding: Interleaving reasoning with actions on an environment beat imitation and RL, and cut hallucination on HotpotQA via a Wikipedia API.
numbers: ALFWorld +34 points absolute; WebShop +10 points; 1-2 in-context examples.
limits: Abstract numbers; the environment is simple.
agent_relevance: The basic situated loop: act, observe, think. The world corrects the model's errors.

source: Hong et al. (2023) MetaGPT
finding: Encoding standard operating procedures into agent role prompts gave more coherent software output than chat-based multi-agent systems.
numbers: No numbers in abstract.
limits: Benchmark figures not read. Social structure here is a fixed pipeline.
agent_relevance: Hutchins-style division of labour with fixed artifacts passed between roles. Procedures act as the shared artifact.

source: Liu et al. (2023) Lost in the Middle
finding: Models use information best at the start or end of context. The middle is used worse, even in long-context models.
numbers: Multi-document QA and key-value retrieval; size of drop not read.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: The layout of the external store changes what the model can use. Put the live item at the edge of the prompt.

source: Packer et al. (2023) MemGPT
finding: Treats context like an OS memory hierarchy, paging data in and out, to work past the window.
numbers: No numbers in abstract.
limits: Quantitative results not read.
agent_relevance: An engineered external memory with control flow; a design for the job humans give to notes.

source: Externalization in LLM Agents: Memory, Skills, Protocols and Harness Engineering (2026)
finding: Review frames agent reliability as moving burdens out of the model into memory, skills, protocols and a harness. Anchors on Norman, with Clark and Chalmers and Kirsh cited.
numbers: No experiments. Lists measuring externalization as future work.
quote: the power of an artifact therefore lies in representational transformation
limits: Only the first third of the text read. Argued, not measured. Rejects strong extended-mind claims.
agent_relevance: Gives the vocabulary for our design view. Confirms nobody has measured how much load moves outside.

source: Sokoban and Tetris LLM harness study (arXiv 2505.15146, 2025)
finding: Adding a harness (symbolic text perception plus memory of states and actions) raised game scores of reasoning models.
numbers: o3 Tetris 31.0 to 42.0, Sokoban 2.0 to 8.0. o1 Tetris 13.0 to 35.0. Random Tetris 10.2. Non-reasoning models near random both ways (gpt-4o 14.7 to 14.0). Claude 3.7 thinking 13.0 to 16.3. 13 models, 3 runs each (o1, o3: 1 run).
limits: Does not test epistemic actions or reliance on the environment. Scores are game-specific units.
agent_relevance: The harness is the environment doing perception work. Gains appear mainly for stronger reasoning models; weak models do not benefit.

source: Annese et al. (2025) Who Sees What? Structured Thought-Action Sequences for Epistemic Reasoning in LLMs
finding: ReAct agents handled simple attention filtering but not occluded spaces or the cost of epistemic actions. Structured examples helped only slightly.
numbers: L-type examples gave slightly fewer clarification requests and steps; no figures in abstract.
limits: Abstract only; inconsistent gains; models not named.
agent_relevance: LLMs do not choose actions to gain information well. Add an explicit step that asks what to look at or ask next.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Toward a Theory of Agents as Tool-Use Decision-Makers
finding: Argues internal reasoning and external actions are equivalent epistemic tools, and tool calls should match the knowledge boundary.
numbers: None known.
limits: Seen only as a search result; not opened.
agent_relevance: Theory support for deciding when to act on the world versus think.

source: Kirsh and Maglio (1994) On distinguishing epistemic from pragmatic action (Tetris)
finding: Tetris players rotate pieces physically to see fit, not only to place them. These are epistemic actions.
numbers: Not retrieved. A 2013 thesis (N=13) found Tetris training without rotation gave no extra mental rotation gain.
limits: Search snippets only; the 300 ms figure was not found.
agent_relevance: Machine analogue: take cheap probing actions in the environment before committing. No LLM study tests this directly (searched, none found).

source: Guingrich et al. (2026) Belief Offloading in Human-AI Interaction
finding: Defines belief offloading as handing the forming and holding of beliefs to an AI.
numbers: None known.
limits: Search snippet only.
agent_relevance: Warns about the cost side of offloading, on the human side.

source: Unlu (2026) Know When to Trust the Skill: Delayed Appraisal and Epistemic Vigilance for Single-Agent LLMs
finding: Single-agent architecture MESA-S with delayed metacognitive evaluation of stored skills; has a preliminary feasibility section.
numbers: Body text unreadable (compressed PDF); only section titles seen. About 7 pages.
limits: Only structure seen, so not counted as opened. Cannot report results.
agent_relevance: Hint that skills pulled from external storage should be checked before trust. Verify before relying.

source: Search negative: LLM tests of manipulatives, ship navigation, epistemic action
finding: Searches for LLM studies reproducing the Martin and Schwartz manipulatives effect, Hutchins ship navigation, or Kirsh epistemic action found none.
numbers: 0 direct hits across 5 web searches.
limits: Web search only; arXiv and Semantic Scholar APIs not tried.
agent_relevance: Gap: the exact paradigms of this subfield have no LLM tests. Transfer from humans is untested.

source: Cross-study pattern (c01, c02, c04, c10, c18)
finding: Across LLM studies, gains from the environment are large when it filters, executes exactly, or stores state, and absent or negative when it only adds volume or talk.
numbers: Positive: SWE-agent 11 to 18%; PAL +15 points; Tetris o3 31 to 42. Negative: full-file viewer 12.7 vs 18.0; CoThinker instruction following 0.95 vs 1.03; weak models flat on harness.
limits: Synthesis by this agent from the lines above, not a new measurement.
agent_relevance: Design rule: the program does exact work (code, checks, storage) and shows the model short, filtered views.
